title: Summative Test 1 — Earth, Greenhouse & Philippine Geology
revision: 2026-11 rev2 — 70:30 LOTS:HOTS, balanced choices, in-scope items only

questions.text: About how much of Earth's surface is covered by water?
What is Earth's average surface temperature?
options: About 15 °C
About −63 °C
About 100 °C
About 464 °C
questions.correct: About 15 °C

questions.text: Why do scientists call Earth's position the habitable (Goldilocks) zone?
options: Water can stay liquid there
The Sun is smallest from there
Planets there have no air at all
Every planet there has life
questions.correct: Water can stay liquid there

questions.text: Which feature protects Earth's atmosphere from being stripped away by the solar wind?
options: The magnetic field
The ozone layer only
The deep ocean water
The Moon's gravity
questions.correct: The magnetic field

questions.text: Why is the ozone layer important for life on land?
options: It absorbs harmful UV rays
It makes oxygen for breathing
It keeps the oceans liquid
It holds the Moon in orbit
questions.correct: It absorbs harmful UV rays

questions.text: Mars has polar ice and signs of old rivers, but no liquid surface water today. Why?
options: It is too cold, with very thin air
It is too hot, with very thick air
It has too much oxygen in its air
It is the planet closest to the Sun
questions.correct: It is too cold, with very thin air

questions.text: Two planets are at the same distance from their star. Planet X has a thick CO₂ atmosphere; Planet Y has almost none. Which is likely warmer, and why?
options: X — its atmosphere traps more heat
Y — no air lets more heat stay in
Both equal — only distance matters
Y — thin air always makes it hot
questions.correct: X — its atmosphere traps more heat

questions.text: A news post says Venus is hot ONLY because it is near the Sun. Which evaluation is BEST?
options: Incomplete — its thick CO₂ air is the main cause
Correct — distance is the only cause of heat
Correct — Venus is the closest planet to the Sun
Incomplete — Venus is actually a cold planet
questions.correct: Incomplete — its thick CO₂ air is the main cause

questions.text: What does the greenhouse effect do?
options: Traps some heat, keeping Earth warm
Blocks all sunlight from reaching us
Makes the ozone layer grow thicker
Pulls carbon dioxide into the soil
questions.correct: Traps some heat, keeping Earth warm

questions.text: Which radiation do greenhouse gases absorb?
options: Infrared
Visible light
Ultraviolet
Gamma rays
questions.correct: Infrared

questions.text: Which source releases large amounts of CO₂?
options: Burning coal, oil and gas
Planting trees and mangroves
Using wind and solar power
Riding bikes and walking
questions.correct: Burning coal, oil and gas

questions.text: Which gas is stronger per molecule than CO₂ and comes from rice paddies?
options: Methane
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Argon
questions.correct: Methane

questions.text: What is albedo?
options: How much sunlight a surface reflects
How much rain a place gets in a year
How deep the ocean is near a coast
How fast the wind blows in a storm
questions.correct: How much sunlight a surface reflects

questions.text: Why is the natural greenhouse effect good for life?
options: Without it, Earth would be too cold
It removes all CO₂ from the air
It makes typhoons much weaker every year
It blocks all UV rays from the Sun
questions.correct: Without it, Earth would be too cold

questions.text: A barangay replaces dark asphalt roofs with white roofs on public buildings. How does this affect heat?
options: More sunlight is reflected, so buildings stay cooler
More sunlight is absorbed, so buildings get warmer
Roof color has no effect on how much heat is absorbed
White roofs release more carbon dioxide into the air
questions.correct: More sunlight is reflected, so buildings stay cooler

questions.text: Arctic ice is melting, and warming there is faster than the global average. Which feedback BEST explains this?
options: Less ice exposes dark water that absorbs more heat
More ice forms and reflects even more sunlight
Melting ice releases cold air that cools the planet
Dark water reflects more sunlight than white ice
questions.correct: Less ice exposes dark water that absorbs more heat

questions.text: What are tectonic plates?
options: Moving slabs of lithosphere
Layers of liquid iron in the core
Clouds of ash above the volcanoes
Flat coral reefs along the coasts
questions.correct: Moving slabs of lithosphere

questions.text: At which boundary does one plate sink beneath another?
options: Convergent (subduction)
Divergent (spreading)
Transform (sliding)
Passive (no motion at all)
questions.correct: Convergent (subduction)

questions.text: What landform forms where an oceanic plate sinks?
options: A deep ocean trench
A wide, flat desert
A mid-ocean ridge
A shallow lagoon
questions.correct: A deep ocean trench

questions.text: What is the Pacific Ring of Fire?
options: A volcano-and-quake belt around the Pacific
A ring of coral reefs near the equator line
A ring of deserts around Australia and Asia
A chain of forest fires in the Pacific islands
questions.correct: A volcano-and-quake belt around the Pacific

questions.text: Which process formed volcanic islands like those in the Philippines?
options: Subduction magma rising and piling up
Coral reefs sinking into deep water
Glaciers carving out large valleys
Rivers dropping mud into the ocean
questions.correct: Subduction magma rising and piling up

questions.text: Rocks in Palawan match rocks of mainland Asia, while Luzon's rocks are younger and volcanic. What does this show?
options: The islands came from pieces of different origins
All Philippine islands formed in one volcanic eruption
Palawan formed from the youngest lava of Mayon
Luzon broke off from Australia only last century
questions.correct: The islands came from pieces of different origins

questions.text: Students must make a cross-section model of how Philippine volcanoes form. Which sequence is MOST accurate?
options: Plate sinks → mantle melts → magma rises → volcano
Volcano forms → magma sinks → plate rises → trench fills
Rain falls → rocks melt → lava cools → ocean forms
Coral grows → reef sinks → plate melts → island floats
questions.correct: Plate sinks → mantle melts → magma rises → volcano

questions.text: Which monsoon brings heavy rain to western Luzon from about June to September?
options: Habagat
Amihan
Trade winds
Land breeze
questions.correct: Habagat

questions.text: Which describes Climate Type IV?
options: Rain spread evenly all year
Six dry months and six wet months
No rain at all during the whole year
Snow in December and rain in May
questions.correct: Rain spread evenly all year

questions.text: Which feature makes the Puerto Princesa Underground River a karst landscape?
options: It flows through dissolved limestone
It flows over cooled volcanic lava
It is fed by melting mountain snow and ice
It was dug by early Filipino miners
questions.correct: It flows through dissolved limestone

questions.text: Why is the Philippines part of the Coral Triangle important?
options: It has the richest marine life
It has the coldest waters on Earth
It has no coral reefs at all
It has the deepest desert in Asia
questions.correct: It has the richest marine life

questions.text: A biologist finds a frog species only on one mountain in Mindanao. How should she classify it?
options: Endemic
Invasive
Extinct
Migratory
questions.correct: Endemic

questions.text: The eastern side of the Sierra Madre is much wetter than its western side during Amihan. What BEST explains this?
options: Moist winds drop rain on windward slopes
The western side is closer to the equator
The eastern side has more volcanoes
The western side faces the wide Pacific Ocean
questions.correct: Moist winds drop rain on windward slopes

questions.text: A province plans to clear a large forest for a new road through Philippine Eagle habitat. Which recommendation is BEST?
options: Reroute the road to keep the forest connected
Proceed — eagles can live in roadside trees
Proceed — forests regrow fully in one year
Reroute — but only to save construction money
questions.correct: Reroute the road to keep the forest connected
